newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council battles with Middle East resolution.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council battles with Middle East resolution.

text.p: After hearing hours of speeches critical of Israel over the latest Middle East crisis, Security Council members failed to agree on a resolution on Saturday but kept negotiating throughout the day.
Consultations, mainly between American, Palestinian and Egyptian diplomats, continued for most of the day in an effort to draft a resolution.

Almost all 50 speakers in the council's public debate on Friday criticised Israel's new right-wing government in varying degrees for opening an archaeological tunnel in the Old City of Jerusalem and accused it of delaying the Middle East peace process.
Whether or not the tunnel should be mentioned in a resolution is one of the main obstacles with the United States objecting and Arab nations insisting it be included.

U.S. ambassador Madeleine Albright told the council: "Let us turn our attention not toward condemnation but toward encouraging the parties to restore the peace process and return to efforts to achieve concrete progress.

"Words here are no substitute for action in the region," she said, alluding to intensive U.S. efforts to arrange a meeting between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to end clashes which have claimed the lives of more than 50 Palestinians and over a dozen Israelis in the past four days.

The violence was sparked by the opening by Israel of a new entrance to an underground passage along the Western, or Wailing Wall, a Jewish holy place, which is near the al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine.
An Arab League statement accused Israel of opening the tunnel as part of a plot to destroy the Aqsa mosque and obliterate Islamic Arab landmarks.
Israel said the tunnel, intended as a window for tourists on 2,500 years of history, was closed on Friday but only temporarily.

A draft resolution proposed by the Security Council's non-aligned members, led by Egypt, would demand the complete closure of the tunnel and call on Israel to cease all acts affecting the safety of the Palestinian people.

It would also call for the immediate resumption of Middle East peace negotiations and the timely implementation of previously concluded agreements. Most speakers in the debate accused Israel of dragging its heels on both counts.
Diplomats said this draft was unacceptable to the United States, which has a veto in the council.

The non-aligned group was said to reject a blander version omitting any reference to the tunnel or criticism of Israel while calling for the cessation of all acts that might aggravate the situation and for an immediate resumption of peace negotiations and the timely implementation of existing accords.
